name: David Hare
role: Education reformer in early colonial Calcutta
contribution: David Hare helped establish Hindu College in Calcutta in 1817 and supported the Calcutta School-Book Society, which published and supplied educational texts in English and Bengali. In 1818 he also helped organize the Calcutta School Society, which aimed to improve existing schools and expand access to useful instruction.
context: A Scottish watchmaker who settled in Calcutta, Hare redirected his time and resources toward education during the city's early nineteenth-century institutional expansion. His work connected Indian reformers, Bengali patrons, and European officials, while remaining focused on schools and learning rather than missionary conversion.
impact: Hare helped build the institutional setting in which later figures such as Henry Derozio and the Young Bengal circle debated education, religion, and inherited authority. His legacy also extended to Hare School and support for Calcutta Medical College, showing how education reform linked schools, textbooks, and public institutions in colonial Calcutta.
highlight: Education organiser behind Hindu College, the School-Book Society, and the Calcutta School Society.
seoTitle: David Hare: Education Reformer in Colonial Calcutta
seoDescription: Explore David Hare's role in founding Hindu College, supporting school-book publishing, and expanding modern education in early nineteenth-century Calcutta.
shortAnswer: David Hare was a Scottish educationist in Calcutta who helped establish Hindu College and school societies that expanded modern education in Bengal.

faq.question: What did David Hare help establish?
faq.answer: He helped establish Hindu College in 1817, supported the Calcutta School-Book Society, and helped organize the Calcutta School Society in 1818.

faq.question: How was David Hare connected to Young Bengal?
faq.answer: Hare helped create the educational institutions and public setting in which the Young Bengal circle emerged, but he was an education organiser and patron rather than the movement's classroom leader.
